newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan steels up on sound outlook and price hikes.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan steels up on sound outlook and price hikes.

text.p: Taiwan's steel shares surged at mid-morning on Wednesday on recent steel price hikes and the expected sound outlook in 1997 triggered by reported sales growth in the domestic property market, brokers said.
With 70 minutes left, steels rose 1.98 percent, while the overall index gained 0.56 percent.
Taiwan's steel giant China Steel rose 80 cents, or 3.02 percent, to T$27.3.
Domestic steel product prices had risen recently and they rose again in April, said Golden Securities research chief Albert Lin.

"Recent newspapers about the rising sales in domestic real estate market also give hope that the steel industry, which relates much to the construction industry, will also benefit from the recovering real estate market," Lin said.

Brokers said construction firms, eyeing signs of a market recovery, had launched aggressive ad campaigns promoting planned residential buildings worth some T$200 billion, hoping to lure homebuyers into their sales rooms during the March 29-30 and April 4-6 holidays.

The United Daily News on Tuesday reported that real estate brokers enjoyed average sales growth of 40 percent in March, with brokers expecting even better performance in April. Other newspapers have similar reports on Wednesday.
